# The change engine

The one way many changes come in at once: a spreadsheet, set-up, the bulk check-in grid, the data tables and MCP.

## The rule

`planChanges(input)` turns rows into a change set: **parse → validate → preview → apply → log**. Nothing is saved until the whole set is valid; then one *commit* saves it all, and one summary entry in the change log can undo all of it.

**The rows.** Each sheet (Goals, Plan, Check-ins, People, Asks) is known by its header row alone; its columns are the one format's, listed in [the export format](../export-format.md) (generated from `src/domain/columns.ts`), and every kind of issue it raises in [the issue kinds](../import-issues.md). A row finds its record by a goal's key (G-12), then its ID; a person by email, then by name when only one person has it; a team by name. A column a row leaves out keeps what the record says, and worked-out columns (status, gap, forecast) are never read. A number counts as changed only when it isn't `sameAsWritten`: the same text, or the same number at the decimal places the export writes it with (a plan week of 0.125 at 2 places is written 0.13, and 0.13 read back is no change), so an export loaded straight back is never a change, on any day. A change to any column that can be changed is applied, or said to be a problem, never quietly dropped.

**Checked by the app's own rules.** A goal row is checked as the goal form checks it; a check-in row is judged by [what a check-in must say](check-in.md) in its own week (a week behind plan needs a cause and a why, and a path to green when the call is behind); a person by the people rules; a row's Action (stop a goal, delete one, mark someone as left) by the removal rules. Only a goal's owner or an admin may change it. A plan change after check-ins started needs a reason (one for the whole set, or the row's own), and keeps the old plan. A check-in for a past week is *backfilled*: dated in its own week, so loading history doesn't make a goal look freshly checked in. One for a week that hasn't happened is refused. One for a week already posted replaces it, with a warning naming whose it was.

**One way to save a check-in** (`postCheckIn`): the check-in screens post through the same judgement, with the draft the form holds and a mode that says how it meets the week's own. `new` is refused when the week has a check-in ("Week 45 already has a check-in. Check in again, or correct it."); `again` adds a second beside it ("Checked in again for week 45: …"); `correct` replaces the week's newest, or adds a week that has none, and needs a reason of at least 10 characters, kept as the entry's first difference ("Why corrected") and summed up as "Corrected week 44: 60% is now 61%" or "Added week 44 later: 61%". A week that has passed takes only `correct`. A correction keeps when the record it replaces was posted, so it never turns a late week into an on-time one, nor the reverse; a correction that changes nothing is refused ("Nothing is different from what week 44 already says."). A post that isn't a correction is no import: no Via mark and no import to undo (Delete this check-in takes it back). A correction is an import of one, undone with the import, and History stops saying the week was corrected once it is. A correction that keeps the number names what it changed instead ("Corrected week 44: still 61%, with a new note"). A reason is words: at least 10 characters, at most 500, with at least three letters ("Say why, in a sentence of at least 10 characters (at most 500), so anyone reading week 44 later knows."). A cycle that has ended can't be corrected at all, by any door: the form, Data's tables, MCP and a workbook loaded later all meet one refusal ("FY26 has ended, so its check-ins can't be corrected."); a workbook that carries them unchanged still loads. A week the ended year has no check-in for can still be added, late, with a reason (Lane, 14 Nov: replacing is refused, adding a missing week is allowed). **One meaning for "correct".** Data's tables and the AI assistant (MCP) replacing a week's check-in correct it the same way: a reason is asked first (the change's reason, kept as "Why corrected"), the summary says "Corrected week 44: …", and the replaced week's time and lateness are kept. A workbook's round trip keeps its own words, except an admin's row that replaces this week's check-in on a goal someone else owns: that corrects it the same way, with a reason (Lane, 14 Nov). **Replacing a check-in keeps who checked in** (Lane, 14 Nov), at every door: a correction or a replacing row changes what the week says, never whose it is. The check-in's author stays its author; the change's actor is whoever replaced it, and History's correction line names them with the reason ("Corrected week 45: 60% is now 61%, by Amara Okafor: “The tracker had last week's number in it”"). Before 14 Nov the form, Data's tables, MCP and a workbook made whoever replaced it the author.

**A batch names its own rows** (backlog BT). A Goals row's **Ref** is a label of the file's own, kept nowhere: **Feeds into ref** on another Goals row, and **Goal ref** on a Check-ins row, name the goal that row adds or changes, so one file (or one `bulk_change`) builds a whole tree, with numbers, before any new goal has a key. A Ref on two rows is Must fix on both (and neither row saves); a ref that no row has, or that names a row that can't be saved, is Must fix on the row that uses it. A row with its own Ref is its own goal, even beside another new row of the same name. An empty ref says nothing: the other columns say what a goal feeds, so an export (where both are empty) loads back unchanged. Leaving a new goal out leaves out the rows that name it by Ref, as by name.

**A row that gives a week.** A Check-ins row with "Back on plan by week" and no Recovery is a plan: the old record's recovery state is read only when the row gives neither, so a correction never loses the week it gives.

**Speed** (import spec, rule 10). No row scans a list: goals by id, key and folded name, people by id, the saved check-ins by goal, and the issues by row are maps built once and kept up as rows are read, and a name one letter out is worked out once per name. Results are the same as a scan's, in the same order. A file costs about what its rows do: in Faro's tests, 5,000 new rows are checked in well under a second, and an unedited workbook of nearly 30,000 rows in about two (`src/domain/importSpeed.test.ts`, with N18's limits of 3, 8 and 20 seconds for 1,000, 5,000 and 30,000 rows). The size limits are in `src/domain/importLimits.ts`: comfortable up to 5,000 rows, and read up to 30,000 rows or 20 MB. `planChangesInChunks(input)` is the same engine a chunk at a time: it yields how far it has got (rows read, and what they would add, change and must fix) every 500 rows, so the import's worker can report progress and stop between chunks; `planChanges` runs it to the end. A file that would change more than 5,000 rows is checked, not saved, and split into parts (`splitTables` in `src/domain/splitFile.ts`): people first, each goal with its plan and check-ins, a goal before the goals that feed into it, and a goal larger than a part on its own.

**What it gives:** the items (each a change to one record, with its field-by-field differences), what was unchanged, the issues (errors that block, warnings to check, notes on how a row was read), whether a reason is needed, counts, and the commit (null while anything blocks). In "create" mode (set-up) every row is new: see "Set-up from a file" below.

**One workspace at a time.** The engine reads one workspace's records and nothing else, so every name, key and ID a row gives is matched within that workspace, and a commit names only that workspace's records: its people, teams, cycle and goals, and a check-in's or an ask's goal. A store keeps it so: a save whose records name a record kept under another workspace (an owner `ownerId`, a team `teamId`, a cycle `cycleId`, a parent goal `parentId`, a check-in's goal `goalId`, an ask's goals `goalIds`) is refused whole, never saved in part; where each workspace is kept apart, a save can only reach its own.

**Which rows make items.** A row that a Must fix stops makes no item: every Must fix on a row's own cells ends that row, and ends **reading** it there. Nothing later in the row's reading order (below) is raised for it, notes included: no Team or Type `default` note after a problem with its owner, no `replaces` after `checkin-incomplete`. A question that leaves its row out (`near-ref`, `near-word`, `other-goal`, `totals-row`, below) ends the reading the same way while it is open. Some are found once a row's item is made, so the item stays (and nothing saves while they are there): a goal on two rows found only as the later row is read (`duplicate`: a row answered “the same” as a goal another row already changes, or, at set-up, a name an earlier row has in the same team or none), where the first row keeps its item and only the later row ends (the same key, ID, or name and Team cell on two rows is found before any row is read, so every such row is named and none makes an item); a goal's link (Feeds into, Feeds into key, Feeds into ID, Feeds into ref: `bad-key`, `ambiguous-ref`, `unknown-ref`, `conflicting-refs`, `loop`; the goal is listed without the link) and a person's own checks on People (`personProblems`: an email that isn't one or that someone has, the only admin). A change to someone else's goal, by someone who isn't an admin, is said once the change is known (`not-allowed`) and makes no item. A question about what a cell means leaves its row out until it is answered: `near-ref` (except on a goal's link, Feeds into, where the goal is listed without the link, as for the link's Must fix), `near-word`, `near-header` and `two-columns`, `other-goal` and `totals-row`. A header question holds its column for every row of the sheet: while it is open the column isn't read, and a Must fix a row then meets on that column still ends the row (no item) but isn't raised, as it waits for the answer; what the row raised before that point stays. So with `near-header` on Target a new number goal's row raises its three notes, its owner's (`by-name`), its team's and its Type's (`default`), and makes no item, and with `two-columns` on Goal a new row ends at its name, before its owner, and raises nothing. Every other question lets the row read on as it says, so its item is listed: `same-goal`, `same-person`, `for-someone-else`, `odd-number`, `no-unit`, `decimal-comma`, `past-stage`, `past-plan`, `feeds-lower`, `plan-question`, `many-admins`, `replaces-others` and `big-removal`. An answer of "Leave these rows out" leaves the row out either way; a note never stops anything.

**The order problems are raised in.** Issues are listed by sheet (Goals, Plan, Check-ins, People), then row; row 1 is the header row, whose questions (`near-header`, `two-columns`) come first. Within one row they keep the order the engine raised them, which is the order it reads: a row that repeats another's key, ID or Ref (`duplicate`) first; then a Goals row's key, ID and Action; whether it is another goal (`other-goal`), a totals row or a goal already here (`same-goal`); its owner (`by-name` once matched by name); its team (`default` when it takes the owner's); Level, Type (`default` when read from the columns), Unit, the numbers (a comma decimal), From and To, the plan's weeks, Limit, Stages and stages already past; State; the goal form's Must fix, a name another goal has (`same-name`) and the form's questions; then, once every Goals row is read, its link (and `feeds-lower`); then the Plan sheet; then each goal's change as a whole (`not-allowed`, `plan-question`); then Check-ins, each row from its goal and week to its number and its parts (`replaces` when it replaces someone's), and `replaces-others` last; then People's own checks, and Stop, Delete and Left as the removal rules judge them (`removal-refused`, and `big-removal` on People). A question about the file as a whole (`many-admins`, `big-removal`, `replaces-others`) is one group raised on **each** row it is about, so the file's first issue is on the first of them; `replaces-others` is raised once every Check-ins row is read, so on each of its rows it comes after that row's own issues. import.csv's `kinds` lists every kind raised, notes too, each once, in that order.

**New IDs.** The engine asks `newId(prefix, hint)` for each record as it makes it, in the order it reads: the People sheet's rows first (a team a row adds, then the person), then the Goals rows in order (a team the row adds, a new goal's stages, one each, then the goal), then each changed goal's change-log entry, then each Check-ins row's check-in and its entry, then each ask a check-in raises or changes and its entry, so the prefixes interleave (one check-in that needs a decision gives `ci_c1`, `chg_c2`, `req_c3`, `chg_c4`), then what the rows' actions write (a stop, a deletion, someone who left) and the asks that follow a goal's new owner, and last the import's summary entry and the import's id. A row that stops before its goal is made asks for no goal ID, though stages it read first have had theirs. The prefixes are `p` (a person), `team`, `st` (a stage), `goal`, `chg` (a change-log entry), `ci` (a check-in), `req` (an ask for a decision or help, the kind a check-in raises), `ask` (a question) and `imp` (the import). The drill gives every prefix one counter, `<prefix>_c<n>` from 1, so a new goal's ID counts every ID asked for before it: three stages and then the goal make `goal_c4`; a new person and three stages, `goal_c5`.

**The order of items.** Goals first, in the order their rows first changed them (Goals rows, then the Plan sheet); then the check-in that records a new goal's past stages as done (its `past-stage` question answered `done`; an update only, since set-up offers only `from-now` and `keep` and never marks a stage done); then check-ins, ordered by their goal's ID (alphabetically, as JavaScript's `localeCompare` orders them) and then by week, not by the sheet's rows, so each week is judged with the weeks before it; then people (People rows in order), teams, the goals a row stops or deletes, and the people marked as left.

**A row that replaces a check-in.** A Check-ins row for a goal and week that has a check-in (the check-in its ID names, else that week's newest) is compared with it column by column: Call (an empty Call counts as the same), Value as a number, Stages, Cause, Why, Why greener, Path to green, Back on plan by week, Needs, Recovery (only when a Path to green is given) and Next step; for this comparison a column the row leaves out takes the saved check-in's value. When every one is the same the row is unchanged and isn't judged again. When any differs the week is judged afresh, as a new check-in would be: with the row's Call, or, with none (an empty Call, or no Call column at all), the call the rules work out, which may not be the call saved. Call is the one column that doesn't keep the saved value then: a Value changed with no Call can move Off track to At risk, and so can a row that changes only Next step (`replaces-others`).

**When a reason is needed.** The change set needs a reason (`needsReason`: row 0's `needs_reason` in changes.csv) when (a) a goal's plan changes (`planChanged`: a number goal's Start, Target, Plan, From or Plan from week, To or Due week and its plan numbers; a range goal's bound, Limit, lower limit and margin; a stages goal's stage names and due weeks; or its type) after its first check-in, and neither its row's Reason nor the import's reason says why; or (b) a check-in row with no Must fix of its own corrects one without a reason of 10 to 500 characters with at least three letters in it (`correctReasonOk`). A row corrects when it replaces a check-in through Data's tables or MCP, when an admin's row replaces this week's check-in on a goal someone else owns (whose the goal is decides, not who posted the check-in), and when it adds a week to a year that has ended. An item's own `needs_reason` differs by kind: a plan item says yes whenever its change needs a reason, given or not (the reason given is its Why); a check-in item only while its reason is missing.

**Set-up from a file** ("create" mode). A change set made in create mode never saves: its commit is always null, and what it would make is in `created` (people, teams, goals, check-ins, asks and the keys issued), which set-up saves as the new workspace. The engine starts from the records it is given: set-up gives it none, so every row is new; the drill's create cases give it the workspace at `builtFor`, whose people, teams and goals stay, are matched as usual, and are a new row's twins (a goal's name the workspace has is "on two rows"). Teams it adds are not items; people are. It never asks `past-plan` (a plan that has already ended is set up as written), and every item's Via is the door the engine is given (`via`), not set by the mode: the drill runs its create cases through `spreadsheet`, so their items say `Spreadsheet`. Everyone counts as an admin while a workspace is set up, a goal keeps the key its row gives, and a new check-in belongs to whoever loads the file (the actor), not the goal's owner: setting up from nothing, that is the first person on People, who becomes the first admin. Replacing a check-in, at any door, keeps who checked in.

**"Count them from this week"** (`past-stage`'s answer `from-now`, `stagesFromNow`) moves every stage of the goal, not only those past: each to this week plus its own week scaled into the weeks left, `week + max(1, round(due × scale))`, where `scale = min(1, (weeks in the year − week) ÷ the latest due week)`, and never past the year's last week. "Keep the weeks as typed" (set-up's other answer) leaves them as written.

**Its sentences, fields and log** are below the rule, read from the code: every sentence it says, kind by kind, with the column and value its group is known by; how a check-in row's missing parts are said together; each item's fields, in order, with the words their values are written in; the columns it reads that no export writes; and the change log's entries.

## Every sentence it says

Each problem, question and note is one of these 234 sentences, read by `src/spec/engineWords.ts` from the engine’s own source (`src/domain/changeset.ts`) and from the rules it shares, where those make the sentence: the goal form’s Must fix and questions (`goalMustFix`, `goalChecks` in `src/domain/goalEntry.ts`), a check-in’s number (`valueProblem` in `src/domain/checkin.ts`), the people rules (`personProblems`) and the removal rules (`src/domain/removal.ts`). `src/spec/engineWords.test.ts` checks that every sentence the conformance cases raise matches one of them, under its kind.

- **{placeholder}**: a value put in: a cell as the row wrote it (`{cell}`), a goal’s or person’s name, a week, a number written as the goal writes it (with its unit, digits grouped: “1,500%”). `{sheet}` is Goals, Plan, Check-ins or People.
- **[words]**: said only sometimes; **{a / b}**: one or the other, as the case is.
- A sentence that takes in another (“Week 45: ” and a number’s problem; “Feeds into ref: ” and why the ref names nothing) is listed whole, once for each sentence it takes in. A person cell the row can’t read is said in the person cell’s own sentence (the rows with sheet `{sheet}`); on People, Takes over’s is “Takes over: ” and that sentence.
- **Group column** and **group value** are the third and fourth parts of the group’s id, `kind:sheet:column:value`, kind by kind: each part is lower-cased with every run of spaces as `-`, and the value is folded first (accents off, “&” as “and”, anything but letters and digits as a space, trimmed). A part with nothing is left empty, so `required-empty:goals:owner:` has no value and `not-allowed:goals::` neither column nor value. The sheet part is the sheet’s name: `goals`, `plan`, `check-ins`, `people`.
- **Headers are lower-cased.** The engine reads a sheet’s headers in lower case (a file’s “Targett” is `targett`), so a sentence that names a header as the row wrote it says it in lower case: “A column on Goals is called “targett”. Read it as Target?”. A column the engine names itself keeps its own words (Target, Owner email).

Where a placeholder could be read more than one way, it is fixed words:

- **{metric, range or milestone}** names all three types, always, in those words; **{columns filled in}** are the groups the row fills (Start and Target; Limit; Stages), joined by “, and ”.
- **{Owner and Owner email}** names the person columns the row gives, in the order Owner, Owner email, Owner ID, and **{name and name}** the people they name in that order.
- **{its column}** of `plan-order` on Goals is the group’s column `due-week`, whichever of To and Due week the row gave.
- **[ {unit}]** after a number in a check-in’s refusal is the goal’s unit after a space, `%` too (“below zero %”), unlike a number written with its unit, where `%` is attached.
- A number’s example in “isn’t a number” is at the goal’s decimal places (“like 29” for a whole-number goal), except Effect’s on a Goals row, which is always the default `29.4`.

Said in full, by the cases that raise them:

| Case | Kind | Group | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| `conflicting-refs` | `conflicting-refs` | `conflicting-refs:goals:owner:` | Owner and Owner ID name different people (Rhea Kapoor and Tunde Bakare). Change just one of them. |
| `type-unclear` | `type-unclear` | `type-unclear:goals:type:` | Type is empty and the row has Start and Target, and Stages. Say metric, range or milestone. |
| `plan-order` | `plan-order` | `plan-order:goals:due-week:` | To (week 10, 2–8 Mar 2026) isn’t after From (week 45, 2–8 Nov 2026). The plan has to run forwards. |
| `to-before-from` | `plan-order` | `plan-order:goals:due-week:` | To (week 40, 28 Sep–4 Oct 2026) isn’t after From (week 46, 9–15 Nov 2026). The plan has to run forwards. |
| `effect-not-number` | `not-a-number` | `not-a-number:goals:effect:` | “lots” isn’t a number. Type digits only, like 29.4. |
| `impossible-number` | `impossible-number` | `impossible-number:check-ins:value:` | Week 45: It can’t be below zero %. |

## What a check-in row lacks, in one sentence

A check-in row that the check-in screen would not post (`checkin-incomplete`) is one sentence: “Week {week} needs ” and every part it lacks, joined by “; ”, in the order the check-in rule finds them (`evaluate` in `src/domain/checkin.ts`), then a full stop. A number that can’t be used is said on its own instead (“Week 45: …”, under `not-a-number`, `precision` or `impossible-number`), and an empty Value as “Week 45 needs a Value.” The group’s value is the same parts, so one answer covers every row that lacks the same.

| Part (the rule’s code) | Said as |
|---|---|
| `value-not-number` | a number in Value |
| `value` | a Value |
| `value-precision` | a Value at the goal’s decimal places |
| `value-impossible` | a possible Value |
| `greener-why` | Why greener (the call is {greener}) |
| `reason-ahead` | a Cause and a Why of 10 characters or more (it’s ahead of plan) |
| `reason-behind` | a Cause and a Why of 10 characters or more (it’s behind plan) |
| `path` | a Path to green and, if it’s a plan, Back on plan by week (after week {week}, by week {weeks in the year}) |
| `story-unchanged` | whether what you said last time is still true |
| `target` | a proposed target beyond the current one |

So a week behind plan, called off track, with no cause, why or path is “Week 45 needs a Cause and a Why of 10 characters or more (it’s behind plan); a Path to green and, if it’s a plan, Back on plan by week (after week 45, by week 53).”

## Field by field

Every item carries the fields it changes as `Field: before → after`, in the order below, each value in the words a person reads; `—` is nothing. A new record lists only the fields it fills (a field that would be `—` is left out); a changed one lists only the fields that differ. These are the change log’s own differences (`goalFields`, `checkInFields` in `src/domain/changes.ts`; `personChange` in `src/domain/people.ts`): the tables are made by running them on the conformance workspace, so each example is what the code writes.

**A goal’s fields**, in this order:

| Field | On | Written as, for example |
|---|---|---|
| Name | every goal | Time from pull request opened to first review |
| State | every goal | — |
| Type | every goal | Move a number |
| Team | every goal | Developer Experience |
| Owner | every goal | Tariq Haddad |
| Feeds into | every goal | Lead time for changes |
| Why it helps | every goal | Most of a change’s lead time is waiting for review, so the first review is where the hours are. |
| Also helps | every goal | — |
| Guarded by | every goal | — |
| Level | every goal | SVP |
| Role | every goal | Input |
| Guardrail | every goal | No |
| Estimated effect | every goal | 8 |
| Data source | every goal | GitHub pull request data |
| Definition | every goal | Median business hours from a pull request being opened (not draft) to its first human or AI review comment |
| Unit | number, range | hours |
| Decimals | number, range | 1 |
| Start | number | 20.0 hours |
| Target | number | 6.0 hours |
| Plan shape | number | Straight line |
| Plan from week | number | — |
| Target due | number | — |
| Plan numbers | number | — |
| Baseline | number | — |
| Limit | range | At most 2.0% |
| Warning margin | range | 0.4% |
| Stages | stages | Vendor contract signed (wk 8), Pilot on the payments monorepo (wk 18), Web monorepo on the merge queue (wk 30), All… |

Its words: State is `Proposed` or `—`; Type is `Move a number`, `Keep a number in range` or `Hit dated stages`; Feeds into is the goal’s name, or `Nothing`; Why it helps is `—` when it feeds nothing; Role is `Input` or `Output`; Guardrail `Yes` or `No`; a number is written as the goal writes it, with its unit (`10%`, `52 hours`, `1,500%`); Target is `Not set` on a proposed goal with none; Plan shape is `Straight line`, `Back-loaded` or `Three steps`; Plan from week and Target due are `Week 45`, or `—`; Plan numbers are `wk 46: 12%, wk 47: 14%`; a range’s Limit is its rule in words (`At most 12%`, `Between 99.5% and 99.95%`); Stages are `Name (wk N)`, by due week, joined by “, ”.

**A check-in’s fields**, in this order:

| Field | On | Written as, for example |
|---|---|---|
| Status call | every goal | At risk |
| Value | number | 9.6 hours |
| Cause | every goal | Something else |
| Note | every goal | The changes to the review rota are working; the number lags them by a week or two. |
| Why greener | every goal | — |
| Path to green | every goal | Keep the current pace; the gap closes at about a point a week. (by week 46) |
| Needs | every goal | Daniel Okafor: agree to run without batching on the web monorepo for a month |
| Proposed target | every goal | — |
| Next step | every goal | — |
| Stages | stages | Vendor contract signed: done wk 8; Pilot on the payments monorepo: done wk 21; Web monorepo on the merge queue:… |

Status call is the status’s word (`On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`); Path to green is what will be done and, in brackets, `by week N` or the recovery’s word in lower case; Stages are `Name: done wk N`, `Name: expected wk N` or `Name: on schedule`, joined by “; ”.

**A person’s fields.** A new person: `Person`, `Email` (Email only when they have one). A person changed, only what differs, in this order: `Name`, `Email`, `Job title`, `Team`, `Admin`; Admin is `Yes` or `No`, and an empty email, job title or team is `—`.

**Beside them**, an item can carry:

| Field | When | For example |
|---|---|---|
| `Why` | A plan change with its reason (the row’s Reason, else the import’s reason), after the record’s own fields; and a goal stopped, with its Reason. | Why: — → Measured the other way round (`plan-question`) |
| `Why corrected` | A check-in a row corrects, with the reason: first, before the check-in’s own fields. | Why corrected: — → The tracker had last week’s number in it (`corrects-keeps-author`) |
| `Status` | A goal stopped (`Stopped`). A deleted goal carries none: its item is `Goal: {name} → —`, then Via. | Status: — → Stopped (`big-removal`) |
| `Open asks` | A goal that changes owner, whose open asks of the old owner go with it. | — |
| `Via` | Every item, last. | Via: — → Spreadsheet (`baseline-provisional`) |

Via is the door, one of `Spreadsheet`, `Bulk edit`, `MCP`, `Data tables`, `Set-up`, `Check-in`: every change through a door but the check-in form carries it, last.

**Whole items**, as the conformance cases make them (changes.csv’s `diffs`). A new goal lists the fields it fills, and also these, whose value is the goal’s own though it reads like nothing: Feeds into (`— → Nothing`), Level, Role, Guardrail, Decimals, Plan shape (a number goal), Warning margin (a range) and Plan from week (this week, when the row gives no From). Target due is left out when it is the cycle’s end. Plan from week and Target due are the bare week of the cycle’s own count, `Week 66` for a week in the next goal year, and so are the weeks in Plan numbers (`wk 4: 60`) and Stages (`Pilot (wk 8)`) ([years and weeks](years-and-weeks.md)). A goal stopped carries Status, then Why, then Via. Baseline is `Baseline, {period}`, then `, provisional` when it is.

| Case | Item | Diffs |
|---|---|---|
| `saves-new-goal` | new goal | Name: — → Runbooks for every paging service \| Type: — → Move a number \| Team: — → CI/CD \| Owner: — → Rhea Kapoor \| Feeds into: — → Nothing \| Level: — → Team \| Role: — → Input \| Guardrail: — → No \| Unit: — → % \| Decimals: — → 0 \| Start: — → 40% \| Target: — → 90% \| Plan shape: — → Straight line \| Plan from week: — → Week 45 \| Via: — → Spreadsheet |
| `saves-stop` | stop goal | Status: — → Stopped \| Why: — → Folded into the platform goal this quarter. \| Via: — → Spreadsheet |
| `baseline-provisional` | new goal | Name: — → A new goal \| Type: — → Move a number \| Team: — → CI/CD \| Owner: — → Rhea Kapoor \| Feeds into: — → Nothing \| Level: — → Team \| Role: — → Input \| Guardrail: — → No \| Unit: — → % \| Decimals: — → 0 \| Start: — → 10% \| Target: — → 50% \| Plan shape: — → Straight line \| Plan from week: — → Week 45 \| Baseline: — → Baseline, June to September 2026, provisional \| Via: — → Spreadsheet |
| `to-next-year` | new goal | Name: — → A new goal \| Type: — → Move a number \| Team: — → CI/CD \| Owner: — → Rhea Kapoor \| Feeds into: — → Nothing \| Level: — → Team \| Role: — → Input \| Guardrail: — → No \| Unit: — → % \| Decimals: — → 0 \| Start: — → 10% \| Target: — → 50% \| Plan shape: — → Straight line \| Plan from week: — → Week 46 \| Target due: — → Week 66 \| Via: — → Spreadsheet |

## Columns it reads beyond the format

The engine also reads 2 columns no sheet in [the export format](../export-format.md) lists, so no export writes them; a file or a tool may give them (read in any case, like every header):

- **Next**: Check-ins: an older name for Next step, read when there is no Next step column.
- **Owner ID**: Goals: the owner by their ID, as Owner email names them by email. With Owner or Owner email beside it, they must name the same person (`conflicting-refs`); an ID no one has is `bad-key` (“There’s no person with ID {cell}.”).

## The change log’s words

The entries a change set writes, and Undo’s, read from the code as the sentences are. A summary entry’s differences are `Via: — → {door}`, then, for a file, `File: — → {its name}` and `Rows: — → {n} changed, {n} unchanged[, {n} left out]`. Undo’s entry has `Import: {the import’s summary} → Undone` and, when rows stay, `Skipped: — → {why each stays}`. A goal’s “Changed …” names its fields in lower case: up to three joined by “, ”, or the first two and “and {n} more”.

| Entry | Words |
|---|---|
| An import’s one summary entry (`action: imported`) | {Loaded a spreadsheet / Changes via MCP / Edited the data tables / Corrected a check-in / Bulk edit}: {{goal} · {summary} / what it counts} |
| What it counts, after the colon (`describe`; nothing: “No changes”) | {n new people}, {n people} changed, {n teams} changed, {n new goals}, {n goals} changed, {n plans} changed, {n check-ins}[ ({backfilled} for past weeks)], {replaced} replaced, {n goals} {stopped}, {n goals} deleted, {n people} {marked as left}, {records}, joined by “, ” |
| A goal added or changed (`goalChange`) | Changed {fields} / Created the goal “{goal}” |
| A check-in posted or replaced (`checkInChange`) | Posted an update for week {week}: {number · status call} / Checked in for week {week}: {number · status call} |
| A check-in a row backfills (an earlier week, not a correction) | {the check-in’s summary} (loaded later) |
| A check-in corrected (`correctedSummary`; a week added to an ended year: “Added week {week} later: {number}”) | Corrected week {week}: {old number} is now {new number} / Corrected week {week}: still {new number}[, with a new {{what changed} and {what changed} / what changed}] |
| A person added or changed (`personChange`) | Changed {person} / Added {person} |
| A team an admin’s file adds, or a team objective changed | Added the team “{team}” / Changed the objective of the team “{team}” |
| Undo’s entry (`action: undone`) | Undid {undone what}: {n rows} put back[, {length} skipped as changed since] |
| What Undo’s entry calls the import (`undoneWhat`) | a correction / the import of {file} / the {import name} |
| Why Undo leaves a row (each `{name}: {reason}`, joined by “; ” in its Skipped field) | {who} posted a check-in[ for week {week}] on {day, as 12 Nov} / The check-in was deleted on {day, as 12 Nov} / The check-in was corrected on {day, as 12 Nov} / Its {field} was changed on {day, as 12 Nov} / It was changed on {day, as 12 Nov} |
| When Undo can put nothing back (`nothingToUndo`) | Nothing left to undo: {its one row has / all {n rows} have} changed since. / Nothing to undo: it changed no rows. |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The engine is large (`src/domain/changeset.ts`). The rule above says what it does and the tables below give every sentence it says and every field it writes, read from its code; a rebuild of the core status rules does not need it, a rebuild of import and bulk edit does.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/changeset.ts](../../../src/domain/changeset.ts): `planChanges`, `postCheckIn`, `records`, `describe`
- [src/domain/columns.ts](../../../src/domain/columns.ts): `sheetKindOf`
- [src/domain/numbers.ts](../../../src/domain/numbers.ts): `sameAsWritten`
- [src/domain/commit.ts](../../../src/domain/commit.ts): `Commit`

## Requirements

- `BULK-IMPORT`: A workbook, a zip of CSVs or one CSV can add or change people, goals, plan numbers and check-ins, including past weeks. Every row is checked with the app’s own rules and previewed before saving; nothing saves while a row needs fixing. Owners change their own goals, admins any, and admins add and change people. Past weeks are marked as loaded later and dated in their own week. Each change is logged on its goal as coming from a spreadsheet.
- `BULK-EDIT`: An owner can type the week’s numbers for all their number goals in one table; each row is judged as they type and asks why only when it is off plan. In the table view, several goals can be selected to change their owner or level, watch or export them, through the same checks and change log.
- `ONE-FORMAT`: One spreadsheet format: every sheet and column is defined once (src/domain/columns.ts), with its header, its meaning, whether it matches the row, can be changed or is worked out, and how it is written and read. The workbook, the zipped CSVs, one CSV, the set-up template, set-up from a spreadsheet, Import, the Data tables, the AI assistant’s tools and docs/export-format.md (checked to be current) are all made from it. Sheets are known by their header rows, never their names; CSV is read in one RFC 4180 pass (quotes, line breaks in a cell, a byte-order mark) and the formula guard’s apostrophe is taken off; worked-out columns use the vocabulary’s words and are never read; a word a column doesn’t know is a problem, never a default.
- `ROUND-TRIP`: Whatever is exported loads straight back as no change: every demo workspace as a workbook and as zipped CSVs, on any day and at any number of decimal places (a number counts as typed only when it differs from what the export wrote), a Data table saved with columns hidden (its key columns are always written, greyed, at the end), and the AI assistant’s export_table into bulk_change. An edited copy applies exactly its edits, a line break or a leading “-” included. Goals are matched by key, then ID, so last cycle’s file still finds its goals; people by email, then a name only one person has, noted in the preview; every column that can be changed counts, and one a table leaves out keeps what the record says.
- `IMPORT-ACTIONS`: A spreadsheet’s Action column stops a goal with check-ins (with a Reason) or deletes one with none, and marks someone as left (their goals, open asks and teams going to Takes over, by email), with the same rules, refusals and consequences as the app (domain/removal), shown in the preview. The import’s Undo puts every one back: the goal live again, the deleted goal restored, the person back with their goals, asks, reviews and teams.
- `IMPORT-UNDO`: Every import, bulk edit and bulk change through MCP is one line in Past imports and one entry in Activity, and can be undone as a whole by whoever made it or an admin. Undo says beforehand which rows have changed since and will stay.
- `DATA-TABLES`: Every person, goal, check-in and plan is in a table anyone can read, search, sort and filter by any column: a value from its list, a number condition, words, or empty; the filters and sort are in the link. Admins type into cells across many rows and tables, review the before and after with any problems, and save them together. Saving goes through the same rules, rights and change log as Import and the AI assistant: a person keeps a unique name and there is always an admin; a past check-in can be corrected, judged by the same rules, and the old and new values are logged. Every record shows its own ID, which never changes.
- `ONE-PER-WEEK`: Owners can check in as often as they like (ad hoc). Every check-in is kept with its time and reason; the latest in a week is that week’s status for reviews, quarters, charts and exports. A second check-in in a week says so, is logged as such and is compared with last week, never with the first. Checking in again and correcting a week are different: a correction replaces the week's newest and needs a reason. Every screen posts a check-in through the same engine as the table, the import and the AI tools.
